messages:
sri: thinking aloud — we should prototype a 'policy-sim' endpoint to canary routing policy changes without touching live traffic. want opinions on scope and interface.

kate: ++ yes. common pain is we ship a policy and only notice weird fallbacks/latency spikes after rollout. a simulator could help catch those early.

aj: curious: do we mean a deterministic simulator that replays sampled traffic, or a sandbox eval that runs synthetic request batches? both have pros/cons.

sri: both. sketch: two modes — 1) replay mode: feed historical request traces (anonymized) through the exact policy eval path; 2) synthetic mode: generate request distribution (seq len, region mix, tenant weights) to exercise tails.

taylor: important: simulator must use the same policy resolution code and compat checks as runtime. otherwise false positives/negatives. but we need an adapter interface so runtime-specific caches/kernels are stubbed out.

aj: interface idea: POST /internal/policy-sim?mode=replay|synthetic body: {"policy_id": "p-123", "trace_id": "s3-sample-2026-03", "seed": 42, "duration_s": 60, "concurrency": 200, "telemetry_opt": "detailed"} returns summary + histogram.

sri: yep. also must tag all emitted telemetry as simulated so it doesn't mix with prod metrics. and we need quick diffs vs baseline policy.

kate: can we run sim against two policies and get delta of routing decisions? i.e., diffs for per-tenant route chosen, penalty changes, and predicted cost/latency delta.

sri: exactly. diffing is the main value prop. The response should include: percent of requests that change route, top N routes affected, expected QPS shift, estimated token-cost delta, and a small sample of deterministic cases where runtime would fallback.

aj: caution: estimated token-cost requires a cost model. we should reuse the Optimize cost profiles (quantization + batching effects). but call it "estimate" and surface confidence band.

taylor: security note: for private deployments we can't upload traces. need a local sim binary or a VPC-only sim endpoint. interface must support both hosted and private: either remote sim job or a containerized sim run.

sri: agree. design: core policy evaluator packaged as a library with a thin shim for runtime vs sim environment. runtime shim interacts with adapters (capacity, region, cached compatibility); sim shim uses synthetic adapters that implement the same interface but return deterministic/stubbed values.

kate: how do we ensure parity between sim adapters and real adapters? small test: run nightly parity tests where sim->real returns are compared on sampled inputs; flag drift.

aj: operationally, sim must not be able to mutate runtime state. sandbox must run in read-only mode; no route reservation or capacity allocation. simulator should also block any fallthrough that would trigger billing.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy-sim service v0.1 queued for staging. CI run 2/2 tests passed. :rocket:

aj: about determinism: RNGs, timestamps, and ephemeral cache keys cause nondeterminism. we should harden by providing a `time_offset_ms` and deterministic RNG seed. also simulate KV cache warm/cold scenarios by pre-populating with typical prefixes.

sri: good call. also simulate batching effects: we should model effective latency under several batching windows and concurrency points. maybe param: batching_profile: "fast|balanced|throughput".

taylor: for policies with region fallbacks, we need to simulate cross-region penalties and failover windows. include simulated region outage scenario param: {"region_down": ["eu-west-1"], "latency_penalties": {"us-east-1": 0}}

kate: UX: console should show a lightweight diff view with clickable example requests and a per-tenant risk score. that helps PMs review before rolling.

aj: API knobs we should expose: simulate=true (non-blocking dry-run on real traffic), simulate_only (no side effects), compare_to (policy_id), trace_sample (s3 path or inline), seed, time_offset, concurrency, batching_profile, region_scenarios.

sri: question for eng-runtime: do we run sim logic inside route-eval service or as a separate sim service that pulls the same policy bundle? pros/cons?

taylor: separate service avoids risking runtime heap/latency regression. but code duplication is risk. preferred: shared lib used by both, runtime calls are hot path optimized; sim service runs same lib but with extra instrumentation.

aj: rollout plan: 1) implement shared evaluator lib with adapter interfaces (2 weeks), 2) sim service prototype using replay mode (2 weeks), 3) integrate console diff + compare (1 week), 4) parity tests and private deployment packaging (2 weeks).

kate: plus UX + docs + guardrails. we should require policy sim pass (no >X% route-changes for tiered traffic) before auto-canary. maybe gate on >99th percentile latency regression threshold.

sri: final open questions: how to surface confidence, what thresholds to recommend as defaults, and whether to allow simulated "hedged" routing (i.e., simulate multiple concurrent route choices) which may not be feasible in prod.

aj: propose we start conservative: no hedging in sim by default, confidence bands from multiple runs, and an opt-in hedged-sim flag for advanced testing.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging run completed. sim-service image pushed to registry: registry.redwood-inference/internal/policy-sim:v0.1

sri: thanks everyone. i'll draft a short RFC with the API and adapter surface. next meeting: sync with eng-runtime and security to finalize adapter contracts.
